# The specification: clauses

Each clause is a small sequential machine (`VbmSimd/Spec.lean`) that says what a word-parallel kernel must compute, one bit position at a time. A clause is **defined** where its machine is
written (its tag `[VS-n]` is in the doc comment) and **discharged** by a theorem whose docstring starts with the same tag. `scripts/spec-check.sh` (Tier 1) fails when a clause has no
definition or no theorem, or a tag is not a clause. Bit `i` is counted from the least significant bit; bytes of a block are read little-endian.

| clause | the machine | the kernel it specifies | discharged by |
|---|---|---|---|
| VS-1 | `scanXor x`: the state after bit `i` is the xor of bits `0 .. i` of `x` | `prefixXor`, `prefixXorC` (the in-string mask from a quote mask, with a carry across blocks) | `prefixXor_spec`, `prefixXorC_spec`, `prefixXorC_carry` (`VbmSimdProofs/PrefixXor.lean`) |
| VS-2 | `escSpec b pb`: byte `i` is escaped iff the byte before it is a backslash that is not itself escaped; `pb` is the carry in | `escaped`, `escOut` (the add-with-carry trick; the carry out of the block) | `escaped_spec`, `escOut_spec`, `quote_not_escaped_spec` (`VbmSimdProofs/Escape.lean`) |
| VS-3 | `laneEq c w k`: byte `k` of `w` equals byte `k` of `c` | `eqLanes`, `zeroLanes` (SWAR compare of eight bytes; flags in the top bit of each lane; nothing else set) | `eqLanes_spec`, `eqLanes_low` (`VbmSimdProofs/Lanes.lean`) |
| VS-4 | `laneFlag m k`: the flag of lane `k` (bit `8k + 7`) of a mask that carries one flag per lane | `pack8` (the eight flags to the low eight bits, one multiply) | `pack8_spec`, `pack8_high` (`VbmSimdProofs/Pack.lean`) |
| VS-5 | the models `ld64Model`, `st64Model`, `st32Model` (`VbmSimd/Shims.lean`): a load reads bytes `i .. i+7` little-endian, zero past the end; a store writes little-endian and nothing past the end | the C shims `vbm_simd_ld64`, `vbm_simd_st64`, `vbm_simd_st32` (trusted; tested against the models) | `ld64Model_bit`, `st64Model_size`, `byteAt0_st64Model_in`, `byteAt0_st64Model_out`, `ld64Model_st64Model_self`, `ld64Model_st64Model_other` (`VbmSimdProofs/Shims.lean`); the shims: `scripts/test-shims.sh` |
| VS-6 | `ctzModel x`: the position of the lowest set bit, 64 for zero | the C shim `vbm_simd_ctz` (trusted; tested against the model) | `ctzModel_spec`, `ctzModel_zero` (`VbmSimdProofs/Shims.lean`); the shim: `scripts/test-shims.sh` |
| VS-7 | `curStream ws n w m`: the set positions of `m`, then of every later word, increasing | `cursorStart`, `cursorNext`, `seek`, `curPos`, `clearLowest` (walk the set bits of a mask array in order with `ctz` and `x & (x - 1)`, no index array) | `cursorStart_spec`, `cursorStart_filter`, `cursorNext_spec` (`VbmSimdProofs/Cursor.lean`) |
| VS-8 | `bit p` of a block mask is `f` applied to word `p / 8`, bit `p % 8` | `mask8` (eight per-word results into one 64-bit block mask), `eqMask64` (the mask of the bytes of a 64-byte block equal to a given byte) | `mask8_bit`, `eqMask64_spec` (`VbmSimdProofs/Mask.lean`) |
| VS-9 | `zeroBytes n`: `n` bytes, all zero | `zeroBytes` (the array a scanner stores its masks into; built by doubling) | `zeroBytes_spec` (`VbmSimdProofs/Bytes.lean`) |
| VS-10 | `nextSet masks j`: the first set bit of the mask array at or after position `j` (the end when there is none) | `nextSet` (one word masked below `j`, then `ctz`; later words only if empty; no state to carry) | `nextSet_spec` (`VbmSimdProofs/Cursor.lean`) |
| VS-11 | `findSpec a s i`: the first index at or after `i` whose byte is in the set `s` (at most four bytes packed in a `UInt32`; `a.size` when none) | `findSwar` (eight bytes per step: `ld64`, four `eqLanes` or-ed, the first flagged lane by `ctz`; the zeros that pad a last partial word cannot win); `findAvx2` (the C shim, 32 bytes per step; trusted, tested against the model), `findNeon` (the C shim for aarch64, 32 bytes per step in 16-byte vectors; trusted, tested against the model) and `findFirstOf` (the AVX2 shim on a CPU that has it, the NEON shim on aarch64, `findSwar` otherwise) | `findSwarGo_spec`, `findSwar_spec`, `findAvx_spec`, `findNeonN_spec`, `findFirstOf_spec` (`VbmSimdProofs/Find.lean`); the shim: `scripts/test-shims.sh` |
| VS-12 | `insetSpec a i s`: the 64-bit mask whose bit `p` is set iff byte `i + p` of `a` exists and is in the set `s` (at most four bytes packed in a `UInt32`); bytes at or past the end give 0 | `inset64` (the C shim `vbm_simd_inset64`, AVX2, two 32-byte loads and one compare per member, or NEON on aarch64, four 16-byte loads; trusted, tested against the model; a consumer calls it only where `hasAvx2 () || hasNeon ()`, its own proved portable kernel otherwise) | `bit_insetSpec`, `inset64_spec` (`VbmSimdProofs/Inset.lean`); the shim: `scripts/test-shims.sh` |
| VS-13 | `appendBytes t a i n`: the bytes `a[i, i + n)` appended to `t` (`ByteArray.copySlice` at the end of `t`) | `appendBytes` (the C shim `vbm_simd_append`: for at most 32 bytes, an unshared `t` with room and a run inside `a`, two overlapping moves and a size update; the runtime's `copySlice` otherwise; trusted, tested against the model) | `appendBytes_spec` (`VbmSimdProofs/Append.lean`); the shim: `scripts/test-shims.sh` |
| VS-14 | `classSpec a i t m`: the 64-bit mask whose bit `p` is set iff byte `i + p` of `a` exists and its class bits (`classByte t`: the byte `v & 15` of the table `t` and the byte `v >> 4` of its second half, and-ed) meet the mask byte `m`; bytes at or past the end give 0; `classifyModel` stores four such masks as the words 0 to 3 of `out` where they fit | `classify64` (the C shim `vbm_simd_classify64`, AVX2: two byte shuffles per 32 bytes of input, one compare per mask; NEON on aarch64: two table lookups per 16 bytes, one `cmtst` per mask; trusted, tested against the model; a consumer calls it only where `hasAvx2 () || hasNeon ()`, its own proved portable kernel otherwise) | `bit_classSpec`, `classify64_spec`, `classify64_size`, `classify_word0` to `classify_word3` (`VbmSimdProofs/Classify.lean`); the shim: `scripts/test-shims.sh` |

Planned clauses (not in the tree yet; each lands with its proof): the UTF-8 validation automaton, the chunking theorem that threads a carry
state through consecutive blocks.

## What a clause does not say

A clause says what the kernel computes, not that it is fast and not that a C compiler or a CPU executes the Lean code as written: those are the trust ledger's (`docs/trust-ledger.md`).
